Phase 1 capture flow (brief §10.4), drafted on the real demo job: the A+ Comfort Club water-heater tune-up at 42 Highland Ave, Somerville.

Top row: Start → Evidence → Work done → Findings. Second row: Confidence → Next step → Owner preview → Submitted. Bottom row: the same submit moment offline (7b), and the Design spec beside it.

Static mockups in the Modernist system (Archivo, #ae1800 on text surfaces, square panels, pill chips). All behavior — autosave, offline queue, soft validation, voice rules, open questions — is written up in the Design spec artboard.

The field shell the capture flow lives inside (brief §10.1–10.2), plus the returned-update re-entry (§12).

Today — route in time order with a now marker; access-blocked stops are pinned above the list as an exception band with a working Request access action, never a normal row. Rows are one full-width tap target (≥96px); swipe right starts capture, swipe left navigates. Bottom tab bar: Today · Search · Mine · Account — the whole field app.

Mine — the tech's own updates by state. A returned update leads the list with the manager's note and one action; the tab badge counts items needing the tech's attention. The review-latency line keeps management honest about §16's four-hour target.

Returned — re-enters the capture shell at the step the return reason points to (Needs photo → Evidence), the note pinned, everything already entered kept, resubmit enabled once the flagged item is fixed.
